models_evaluated: commercial AI-based CAD software for chest radiographs

links.outcome: Detection rate of actionable lung nodules on chest radiographs, AI vs non-AI arm, randomized
links.effect: Detection rate 0.59% (31/5238) in AI group vs 0.25% (13/5238) in non-AI group; OR 2.4; 95% CI 1.3, 4.7; P = .008. Malignant nodule detection 0.15% vs 0.0%.
links.quote: The trial met the predefined primary outcome, demonstrating an improved detection rate of actionable nodules in the AI group compared with the non-AI group (0.59% [31 of 5238 participants] vs 0.25% [13 of 5238 participants], respectively; odds ratio, 2.4; 95% CI: 1.3, 4.7; P = .008).

links.outcome: Radiologist performance with versus without AI assistance in the intended deployment mode
links.effect: Radiologists referring to AI results detected more actionable nodules (0.59% vs 0.25%) with similar false-referral rates (45.9% vs 56.0%, P = .14) and positive-report rates (2.3% vs 1.9%, P = .14).
links.quote: The AI and non-AI groups showed similar false-referral rates (45.9% [56 of 122 participants] vs 56.0% [56 of 100 participants], respectively; P = .14) and positive-report rates (2.3% [122 of 5238 participants] vs 1.9% [100 of 5238 participants]; P = .14).

screen.reason: This pragmatic randomized controlled trial prospectively evaluated clinical outcomes with vs without AI assistance for radiologists interpreting chest radiographs in a live health screening workflow.
